transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

It's good to meet you too. Um, what brings me in is... I just can't keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I'll start talking about an overnight shift at work, and then I just end up jumping to soccer, or paint colors, or patient charts. And I can see everyone getting lost while I'm talking. It's just really hard to make sense right now.
Have you been feeling unusually energized lately?
No, not at all. Um... I haven't noticed anything like that. I definitely don't feel energized lately. If anything, it's been the exact opposite.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?
No, um... I haven't heard any voices or anything like that. It's really just my own thoughts. I don't hear anyone talking when I'm by myself.
Have you been feeling like people are trying to harm you or plot against you?

Yeah, actually. I mean... I'm sure the supervisors at work are doing things against me. They changed my shifts, and I know they watch me through the unit cameras to see if I'm being unsafe. People keep telling me it's just because of staffing shortages, but I'm sure that's not it. I know they're watching me.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah, pretty much every day. From the time I wake up, I just feel... really heavy and empty. It doesn't really go away. After my shifts, I'll usually just sit out in my car crying for a while before I can even get it together to drive home.
Have there been times when you felt sure your supervisors were watching or targeting you even when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah, actually. There was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't in that deep, depressed place. I felt a bit better... but I still believed the cameras and the supervisors were monitoring me. I kept acting really guarded at work during that whole time. So, yeah, even when the heavy feeling lifted for a bit, I still knew they were watching me.
Did these problems with your thoughts and the feeling that your supervisors were watching you come on very suddenly?

No, it wasn't suddenly. It just kind of... built up over time, I guess. I didn't just wake up one day and think they were doing it. It was more like I started noticing little things here and there, and then it just became obvious what was really going on.
Have you found yourself caring much less than usual about seeing people or doing things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, definitely. I used to do a lot of things... I'd sketch murals, cook for my friends, play soccer on the weekends. But now, all of that just feels completely pointless. I don't even want to try. I usually just ignore any messages I get and stay in my apartment.
Was there ever a time when you still felt watched or monitored, but you were not feeling depressed at all for at least two weeks?

Yeah, like I mentioned earlier, there was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't feeling depressed. I felt okay... but I still believed the cameras and supervisors were monitoring me. I kept acting really guarded at work during that whole time. So, yes, it lasted for at least two weeks where I wasn't depressed but still knew they were watching me.
For at least one month, have you had the feeling that your supervisors were watching or targeting you?

Yeah, it's been going on for way longer than a month. I'm... I'm absolutely sure the supervisors changed my shifts around on purpose. They watch me through the cameras on the unit, just waiting to see if I do something unsafe. People keep telling me it's just because of staffing shortages, but... I know what's really happening.
For at least one month, have you been having this problem where your speech gets jumbled and hard for other people to follow?

Yeah, it's been at least a month. I just... I can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I'll start talking to someone about an overnight shift, and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, or paint colors, or patient charts. It just gets all mixed up. I can see everyone getting lost when I try to explain things, but I just can't keep my thoughts straight.
Have you found it hard to show much emotion on your face or in your voice lately?
No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any change in how I show emotion. People haven't said anything about my face or my voice being flat or anything like that.
Have these problems overall been going on for at least 6 months?

Yeah, definitely longer than six months. It's been about a year and five months, actually. It all started right after work switched my schedule around. I went from having steady day shifts to doing rotating nights and a lot of overtime, and... yeah, that's when all this really began.
